375479.title: Collapse conjecture for bounded-active-coordinate Hales–Jewett numbers
375479.literal_statement:
Let $\mathrm{HJ}^{[K]}(t,r)$ be the least dimension forcing a monochromatic combinatorial line with at most $K$ active coordinates, and let $\mathrm{HJ}(t,r)$ be the ordinary Hales–Jewett number.

**Collapse conjecture.**

$$
\mathrm{HJ}^{[\mathrm{HJ}(t,r)-1]}(t,r)=\infty
$$

for all $t\geq 2$ and $r\geq 2$.

Thus, even though dimension $\mathrm{HJ}(t,r)$ forces a monochromatic line without an active-coordinate restriction, the conjecture predicts that no uniformly bounded threshold exists when the allowed number of active coordinates is fixed at $\mathrm{HJ}(t,r)-1$. The supplied source context gives no resolution of this claim.

378961.title: The solvable-radical sequence conjecture for finite groups
378961.literal_statement:
Let $G$ be a finite group, and let $R(G)$ denote its solvable radical. Suppose $(u_n(x,y))_{n\geq 1}$ is a sequence of group words in two variables.

**Solvable-radical sequence conjecture.** There exists a sequence $u_n(x,y)$ such that $R(G)$ coincides with the set of elements $y\in G$ having the property that, for every $x\in G$, there is an $n$ for which

$$
u_n(x,y)=1.
$$

Here the sequence is intended to characterize the solvable radical uniformly for each finite group through the vanishing of one of its words for every choice of $x$.

The source states this as a conjecture whose validity would imply the finite-group characterization $S(G)=R(G)$, where $S(G)$ is the set of radical elements. No resolution is supplied in the given text.

378975.title: Three-bases reduction conjecture for Rota's basis conjecture
378975.literal_statement:
Let $M$ be a matroid of rank $n$ on $3n$ elements that is a disjoint union of $3$ bases. Let $I_1, I_2, \ldots, I_n$ be disjoint independent sets of $M$, with $0 \le |I_i| \le 3$ for all $i$. **Three-bases reduction conjecture.** There exists an $n\times 3$ grid $G$ containing each element of $M$ exactly once, such that for every $i$, the elements of $I_i$ appear in the $i$th row of $G$, and such that every column of $G$ is a basis of $M$.

The paper presents this as the three-bases conjecture from which Rota's basis conjecture follows. Its resolution status is not specified in the supplied text.

377304.title: Extreme rays and diameter conjecture for the oriented-multicut skeleton
377304.literal_statement:
Let $QMET_n$ be the cone of quasi-semimetrics and $OMCUT_n$ the cone generated by oriented multicuts. Let $G_{OMCUT_n}$ be the skeleton graph of $OMCUT_n$, whose nodes are its extreme rays and whose edges join adjacent extreme rays. A **dominating clique** is a complete subgraph such that every node is adjacent to at least one of its elements.

**Oriented-multicut skeleton conjecture.** (i) All oriented multicuts are extreme rays of $QMET_n$. (ii) The oriented cuts form a dominating clique in $G_{OMCUT_n}$; consequently, the diameter of $G_{OMCUT_n}$ is $2$ or $3$ for every $n\geq 4$.

The assertions were presented as conjectural general results about the oriented-multicut cone; the surrounding text does not provide a general proof or resolution.

377106.title: Stembridge's polynomial-counting conjecture for nondegenerate sparse symmetric matrices
377106.literal_statement:
Let $G$ be a simple graph with vertex set $V(G)=\{v_1,\ldots,v_n\}$. Let $Z^o_G$ be the scheme of nondegenerate symmetric $n\times n$ matrices $M$ satisfying

$$
M_{ij}=0\quad\text{if }i\ne j\text{ and there is no edge from }v_i\text{ to }v_j.
$$

Equivalently, for a graph $G^*$ obtained from $G$ by adjoining an apex vertex connected to every vertex, the source identifies $Z^o_G$ with $X_{G^*}$. **Stembridge's conjecture.** For every simple graph $G$, $[Z^o_G]$ is a polynomial in $q$. Since it would follow from Stanley's reformulation, and that reformulation is equivalent to the refuted Kontsevich conjecture, this conjecture is also refuted.

319844.title: The totally decomposable word conjecture
319844.literal_statement:
Let $w$ be a finite word in the alphabet $\{X,A\}$. A word is **totally decomposable** if it is the image of $X$ under a composition of maps $\pi_{m,k}:u\mapsto (uA^k)^m u$ for $m\geq 1$, $k\geq 0$, together with $r:u\mapsto uA$ and $l:u\mapsto Au$. A word is **universal** if, for every uniquely divisible group $G$ and every $A,B\in G$, the equation $w(X,A)=B$ has a solution $X\in G$; it is **uniquely universal** if that solution is always unique. A solution is **in terms of radicals** when it is obtained by the radical operations defined for the free uniquely divisible group in the paper.

**The totally decomposable word conjecture.** The following are equivalent: $w$ is totally decomposable; $w$ is uniquely universal; $w$ is universal; and $w(X,A)=B$ has a solution in terms of radicals.

The implications from total decomposability to unique universality and from unique universality to universality, as well as the equivalence with radical solvability, are straightforward. The difficult implication is that radical solvability forces total decomposability; the authors verified the conjecture computationally for words of length at most $10$.

320403.title: Combinatorial tiling conjecture for paired non-acyclic graphs
320403.literal_statement: Let $G=(V,E)$ be a non-acyclic graph, with a fixed-point-free involution $\mu:V\to V$ and, for every vertex $v$, a bijection $\sigma_v:\delta(v)\to\delta(\mu(v))$. Assume that $\lambda(v,\mu(v))=\deg(v)$ and $\sigma_{\mu(v)}=\sigma_v^{-1}$. **Tiling conjecture.** There exists a nonempty list of cycles of $G$ such that, for every pair of edges $e$ and $f$ incident with a vertex $v$, the number of listed cycles containing both $e$ and $f$ equals the number containing both $\sigma_v(e)$ and $\sigma_v(f)$. If $G$ has a connected component with at least four vertices, the list may moreover be required to contain a cycle of length greater than two. This is the combinatorial restatement of the paper’s tiling conjecture and is intended to provide the graph-theoretic structure needed for polygonal surface constructions.

318410.title: Big line or big clique conjecture for planar point sets
318410.literal_statement:
Let $P$ be a finite set of points in the plane. Two distinct points $v,w\in P$ are **visible** with respect to $P$ if

$$
P\cap\overline{vw}=\{v,w\},
$$

where $\overline{vw}$ is the closed line segment between $v$ and $w$. The visibility graph of $P$ has vertex set $P$, with two distinct points adjacent exactly when they are visible.

**Big line or big clique conjecture.** For all integers $k$ and $\ell$ there is an integer $n$ such that every finite set of at least $n$ points in the plane contains either $\ell$ collinear points or $k$ pairwise visible points; equivalently, its visibility graph contains a $k$-clique.

This conjecture predicts a dichotomy between arbitrarily large collinear subsets and arbitrarily large cliques in the visibility graph of a planar point set. The source attributes it to KPW; its resolution is not established by the supplied context.

318509.title: Two-partition conjecture for high-chromatic digraphs and path families
318509.literal_statement:
Let $\mathcal{P}_{3k,k-1}$ be the family of paths used in the source, and let a partition into two sets be written as

$$
\mathcal{P}_{3k,k-1}=\mathcal{Q}_1\mathbin{\dot\cup}\mathcal{Q}_2.
$$

A digraph $G$ admits a homomorphism from a path $P$ when there is a directed graph homomorphism $P\to G$. **Two-partition path conjecture.** There exists a number $C$ such that, for every $k$ and every such partition, one of the sets $\mathcal{Q}_i$ has the property that, for every digraph $G$ with $\chi(G)\geq C$, there is a path $P\in\mathcal{Q}_i$ admitting a homomorphism to $G$.

The claim concerns a uniform chromatic threshold for one side of every two-partition of the relevant path family. The source presents it as an application of the Poljak–Rödl/Hedetniemi topic; no resolution is supplied in the excerpt.

318996.title: The blow-up conjecture for globally rigid graph constructions
318996.literal_statement:
Let $G$ be a connected graph with $v>1$ vertices, denoted $v_1,\ldots,v_v$. Replacing each vertex $v_i$ by an independent set of size $a_i$ and connecting the new independent sets according to the edges of $G$ gives a graph constructed from $G$ by independent-set blow-ups.

**Blow-up conjecture.** For any connected graph $G$ with $v > 1$, there exists some $a_1, a_2, \ldots, a_v$ and some $d$ such that if we replace each $v_i$ with an independent set of size $a_i$ and connect them accordingly, the resulting graph is GPR in $\mathbb{R}^d$.

This conjecture proposes a globally rigid construction for every connected graph with more than one vertex, extending the paper's experimentally observed and proved examples for irreducible graphs of small order, $k$-chains, and $k$-rings. The general assertion remains open in the supplied text.

317807.title: Alev's uniqueness conjecture for simple graphs solving the B_n equation
317807.literal_statement:
Let $B_n$ be the type-$B_n$ case, and let $S^W_{\mathfrak{sl}_2}$ be represented by graphs, with polynomials of degree $4(n-1)$ corresponding to linear combinations of graphs with $n-1$ edges. Consider the equation referred to in the source as Equation. A **simple graph** is the graph formed from the linear graph without loops or isolated vertices, with $n-1$ edges and $n$ vertices, together with corrective graphs having the same number of edges and non-isolated vertices.

**Simple-graph uniqueness conjecture.** For every integer $n\geq 2$, there exists a unique polynomial of degree $4(n-1)$ in $S^W_{\mathfrak{sl}_2}$ solving the equation. It is represented by the $n$th simple graph.

This conjecture concerns the proposed canonical solution at the top relevant degree and its graph-theoretic form. The source gives the construction and terminology but does not state a general proof.

316508.title: The main conjecture on 2-adic valuations of Stirling numbers
316508.literal_statement:
Let $S(n,k)$ denote the Stirling number of the second kind, and for fixed $k\in\mathbb{N}$ partition the integers $n\geq k$ into residue classes modulo $2^m$. A class is **constant** if the values of $\nu_{2}(S(n,k))$ on it consist of a single value; the $m$-level is formed by the non-constant classes modulo $2^m$. Define $m_{0}=m_{0}(k)\in\mathbb{N}$ by

$$
2^{m_{0}-1}<k\leq 2^{m_{0}}.
$$

**Main conjecture.** The first index for which there is a constant class is $m_{0}-1$: every class is part of the $j$-level for $1\leq j\leq m_{0}-2$. For every $m\geq m_{0}$, the $m$-level consists of $2^{m_{0}-2}$ classes, and each produces a single non-constant class for the $(m+1)$-level, so the number of classes at each level remains constant. The conjecture is supported by the examples in the paper, and the special case $k=5$ is established there.

379104.title: The classification conjecture for surgery in the kernel of a colouring
379104.literal_statement:
Let $p$ be an odd prime, let $(K,\rho)$ be a $p$-coloured knot, and consider equivalence classes of $p$-coloured knots under $\pm1$-framed surgery along loops in $\ker\rho$, called **surgery in $\ker\rho$**. The invariant of the paper is defined on these equivalence classes.

**Classification conjecture.** The invariant is a complete invariant of the set of equivalence classes modulo surgery in $\ker\rho$. Equivalently, the theorem asserting that there are exactly $p$ equivalence classes, represented by connect-sums of $n$ left-hand $(p,2)$-torus knots with a given colouring for $n=1,2,\ldots,p$, holds for every odd prime $p$.

The paper proves this classification for $p=3$ and $p=5$; the conjecture extends the result to all odd primes. The proposed invariant is intended to distinguish the $p$ representative classes.

377491.title: The Wide Partition Conjecture for free matroids
377491.literal_statement:
Let $\lambda$ be an integer partition. A **wide partition** is one for which every subpartition $\mu\subseteq\lambda$ dominates its conjugate $\mu'$; equivalently, $\mu\geq\mu'$ in dominance order for every subpartition $\mu$. A tableau of shape $\lambda$ is a filling of its Young diagram with integers.

**The Wide Partition Conjecture for free matroids.** An integer partition $\lambda$ is wide if and only if there exists a tableau of shape $\lambda$ such that (1) for every $i$, the entries in the $i$th row are precisely the integers from $1$ to $\lambda_i$ inclusive, and (2) for every $j$, the entries in the $j$th column are pairwise distinct.

This is the free-matroid case of the broader Wide Partition Conjecture, which is connected to Rota's basis conjecture. The claim had been verified by computer for partitions with at most 65 cells and for partitions whose diagrams fit inside a $10\times10$ square, but no general proof is given here.

377336.title: The Ramsey-ordering conjecture for permutation group orbits
377336.literal_statement:
Let $G$ be a permutation group on $\Omega$ with no finite orbits. Assume that the orbits on $n$-sets can be Ramsey ordered for every positive integer $n$. For positive integers $m$ and $n$, let $c_\alpha$, with $\alpha\in\mathcal{A}$, be a Ramsey ordering of the orbits on $(m+n)$-sets with $N\ge 2(m+n)$, and let $X_\alpha\subseteq\Omega$ be corresponding sets. Suppose this ordering induces Ramsey orderings $d_\beta$, with $\beta\in\mathcal{B}$, and $e_\gamma$, with $\gamma\in\mathcal{C}$, on the $m$-set and $n$-set orbits, respectively. Define $\beta\vee\gamma$ as the least index of an $(m+n)$-set orbit containing a $d_\beta\cup e_\gamma$ decomposition.

**Ramsey-ordering conjecture.** There exists such a Ramsey ordering for which, for all $\beta,\beta'\in\mathcal{B}$ and $\gamma,\gamma'\in\mathcal{C}$,

$$
\beta\vee\gamma<\beta'\vee\gamma\quad\text{if }\beta<\beta'\quad\text{and}\quad\beta\vee\gamma<\beta\vee\gamma'\quad\text{if }\gamma<\gamma'.
$$

This conjecture seeks a compatible ordering of orbit decompositions that is strictly increasing in each component. The paper presents it as the main conjecture in the Ramsey-ordering section; no general resolution is given in the supplied text.

380274.title: The genus-one product identity for the character-variety generating function
380274.literal_statement:
Let $a$ and $l$ be the arm- and leg-lengths of each box in a partition $\lambda$, and let $T,z,w$ be formal variables. The sum is over all partitions, and the product on the left is over all boxes in the Ferrers diagram.

**Genus-one product identity.**

$$
\sum_\lambda\prod\frac{\left(z^{2a+1}-w^{2l+1}\right)^2}{(z^{2a+2}-w^{2l})(z^{2a}-w^{2l+2})}T^{|\lambda|}=\prod_{n\geq1}\prod_{r>0}\prod_{s\geq0}\frac{(1-z^{2s+1}w^{-2r+1}T^n)^2}{(1-z^{2s}w^{-2r+2}T^n)(1-z^{2s+2}w^{-2r}T^n)}.
$$

This identity is a consequence of the main conjecture in the genus-one case, where the character variety is a two-dimensional torus; it is not presented as independently proved in the supplied text.

322399.title: The small-order extremal conjecture for subcube intersection graphs
322399.literal_statement:
Let $C_d$ be the family of subcubes of $\\{0,1\\}^d$, and for a subcube $x\in C_d$ let $F(x)\subseteq[d]$ denote its fixed-coordinate set. Let $\mathcal{I}(n,d)$ be the family of intersection graphs of $n$ subcubes in $C_d$, and let $K_{r+1}$ denote the complete graph on $r+1$ vertices.

**Small-order extremal conjecture.** For any $n\leq 2\times2^{d/2}+(r-2)$, the maximum number of edges in a $K_{r+1}$-free graph in $\mathcal{I}(n,d)$ is attained by a graph $G$ which is a subgraph of a graph $H$ with

$$
V(H)=\{x\in C_d:F(x)=P_i\},
$$

where $P_1,\dots,P_r$ is a partition of $[d]$.

This conjecture asserts that, for the indicated small range of $n$, an extremal $K_{r+1}$-free intersection graph comes from an $r$-partite construction based on a partition of the coordinate set. The paper presents this as the natural extremal construction following the relevant Turán-type examples; no resolution is supplied here.

371478.title: Ore-type conjecture for all orientations of Hamilton cycles
371478.literal_statement: An **oriented graph** is a directed graph with at most one directed edge between any pair of vertices. For an oriented graph $G$, let $V(G)$ be its vertex set, let $n=|V(G)|$, and write $\sigma_{+-}(G)$ for the minimum, over all directed edges $u\to v$, of $d^+(u)+d^-(v)$. An **orientation of an undirected Hamilton cycle** is obtained by assigning a direction to every edge of a Hamilton cycle on $V(G)$; saying that $G$ contains all possible orientations means that it contains a copy of every such orientation. **All-orientations conjecture.** There exists an integer $n_0$ such that every oriented graph $G$ on $n\geqslant n_0$ vertices with $\sigma_{+-}(G)\geqslant(3n+2)/4$ contains all possible orientations of a (undirected) Hamilton cycle. The problem asks whether this Ore-type condition forces every orientation pattern of a spanning cycle, extending Hamiltonicity results beyond a single prescribed cycle orientation.

396838.title: Entringer–Tout Conjecture for prime-labeled trees
396838.literal_statement: Every tree is prime, where a graph $G$ of order $n$ is prime if there is a bijection $f:V(G)\to [n]=\{1,\ldots,n\}$ such that the labels assigned to the endpoints of every edge of $G$ are coprime.

327072.title: Nash-Williams's Hamilton cycle packing conjecture
327072.literal_statement:
Let $G$ be a graph on $n$ vertices, let $\delta(G)$ denote its minimum degree, and let $\operatorname{reg}_{\operatorname{even}}(G)$ denote the degree of a largest even-regular spanning subgraph of $G$.

**Nash-Williams's conjecture.** Suppose that $G$ is a graph on $n$ vertices with minimum degree

$$
\delta(G)\ge n/2.
$$

Then $G$ contains $\operatorname{reg}_{\operatorname{even}}(G)/2$ edge-disjoint Hamilton cycles.

This conjecture would simultaneously generalize the Hamilton decomposition and Hamilton cycle-packing results discussed in the paper, and would give a best-possible bound for each graph rather than only for graphs with a prescribed minimum-degree class. The source records that it was proved for $\delta\ge(2-\sqrt{2}+\varepsilon)n$, so the full statement remains open in the supplied context.
